name: Buy proppant and manage rail supply
summary: Frac sand is the largest material the company pumps, about 1.3 million tonnes a year, and most of it comes by rail from Wisconsin or northern mines to in-basin terminals near the pads. For each planned pad the logistics coordinator decides which terminal will feed it and how much must be released from a term supply agreement, the procurement specialist places the release, and the coordinator tracks the railcars for two to three weeks until the sand is in the terminal silos and allocated to the pad. Rail delays in cold weather, supplier allocation cuts and customer schedule changes leave one terminal short and another full, and every sand plan is kept in spreadsheets fed by portals and emailed reports.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed Canadian pressure pumper with about 1,350 employees, six to eight 24-hour frac crews, a 70-person supply chain department in Calgary and at district bases, an ERP with procurement and inventory, and spreadsheets, email and phone for day-to-day logistics.
baseline.notes: Some customers buy sand directly, which lowers release volume but not hauling; 2020 volumes sit at the low end of the ranges.

unit_of_work: one proppant release (sand for one pad or terminal top-up, typically 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes)
trigger: A new or revised pad program needs sand, or a supplier ships scheduled cars under a take-or-pay agreement.
end_state: The sand is in an in-basin terminal, accepted, allocated to a pad and handed to sand hauling, and the supplier and freight invoices are cleared; or the sand is held in the terminal for a later pad.

volume.seasonality: Highest from January to mid-March, lowest during spring break-up (April to May); 2020 was far below the mode.

evidence.note: About 112,000 tonnes a month (organisation file driver) divided by 2,000-3,500 tonnes per release, less customer-supplied sand. Comparable pumper volumes in step_2021 (1,012,000 tonnes in 2021).

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same winter peak as the organisation file process entry; multiplier is the author's estimate.
Fourteen coordinators in the organisation file cover rail, hauling and fuel around the clock; about two FTE on rail and terminal planning is the author's estimate.
One buyer equivalent on sand releases, claims and invoice queries; author's estimate.
Approvals and rebalancing decisions; author's estimate.
Receipt posting and terminal inventory reconciliation. Not listed for this process in the organisation file process map.

systems.name: ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Rail carrier and sand supplier railcar tracking portals
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)

steps.name: Receive pad proppant requirement
steps.description: The logistics coordinator opens the proppant requirement sent by the frac operations coordinator for a newly planned or revised pad: tonnes by mesh size (for example 100 mesh and 40/70), pad location, planned start date and pumping days. They log it as a new line in the sand plan workbook.

error.defect_description: Tonnes or mesh copied wrongly from the pad program.

evidence.note: Frac service includes procurement and coordination of proppants for each program (trican_frac); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check terminal stock and railcars in transit
steps.description: The coordinator looks up current silo inventory by mesh at each in-basin terminal from the terminal operators' daily reports and the railcars already loaded or rolling in the rail tracking portals. They compare what is free against tonnes already promised to other pads.
outputs: available stock by terminal and mesh

error.defect_description: Stale terminal report leaves stock overstated.

evidence.note: In-basin unit-train terminals hold sand close to the pads (source_q4_2018, source_home); the check itself is the author's description.

steps.name: Build sourcing plan for the pad
steps.description: The coordinator decides which terminal will feed the pad, how many tonnes come from stock already in basin and how much must be released from a supply agreement, and when it must ship from the mine to arrive two to three weeks later. The decision balances truck haul distance from each terminal against the stock left for other pads.
inputs: available stock by terminal and mesh

error.defect_description: Wrong terminal or timing chosen, leaving the pad short or the terminal over-full.

next.condition: new release from a supply agreement needed
covered by stock already in basin

evidence.note: Share covered from in-basin stock is the author's estimate; the trade-off is described in the organisation file process description.

steps.name: Check supply agreement position
steps.description: The procurement specialist opens the term supply agreement tracker for the chosen supplier and checks committed tonnes left this year, any take-or-pay shortfall, the current price and fuel or rail surcharges, and the supplier's monthly allocation by mesh.

error.defect_description: Out-of-date price used on the release.

evidence.note: Sand is sold to pressure pumpers and producers under term contracts that were repriced in 2022 (source_q4_2018, source_q4_2022).

steps.name: Create release purchase order
steps.description: The procurement specialist creates a release against the blanket purchase order in the ERP: tonnes, mesh, origin, destination terminal, ship window and price. They attach the sourcing plan and note the pad and customer so freight and sand costs can be charged to the job.

error.defect_description: Wrong quantity, mesh or destination terminal keyed.

next.condition: above buyer limit or spot purchase outside the agreement

evidence.note: Blanket order and release practice is the author's description of common ERP procurement; approval share is an estimate.

steps.name: Approve release over buyer limit
steps.description: The supply chain manager reviews the release in the ERP approval queue, checks it against the pad's planned tonnes and the supply agreement, and approves it or sends it back with a question.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for purchase commitments

evidence.note: Delegation of authority is standard for listed companies; thresholds and wait are estimates.

steps.name: Send release to sand supplier
steps.description: The procurement specialist emails or uploads the release to the supplier's order desk and phones to agree the load window at the mine or origin transload. They record the agreed ship week in the sand plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Supplier confirms allocation and ship date
steps.description: The sand supplier's order desk checks mine production and its own allocation commitments by mesh and confirms tonnes and a ship date, or offers less sand or a later week.

next.condition: short on a mesh or later date offered

evidence.note: Allocation cuts are common in a peak winter; share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve supplier shortfall
steps.description: The procurement specialist calls other contracted suppliers for the missing mesh, asks the design engineer whether an alternative mesh is acceptable, or accepts a later ship date if the pad timing allows. They update the sand plan with the choice.

error.defect_description: Substitute mesh accepted without a design check.

next.condition: new release to an alternative supplier

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Supplier loads railcars and issues bills of lading
steps.description: The supplier loads covered hopper cars at the mine or origin transload, weighs them and sends the car numbers and bills of lading. A unit train or block of cars then waits for the railway to lift it.

error.defect_description: Car list does not match tonnes released.

evidence.note: Unit trains of 110-120 cars of about 100 tonnes each (aogr_last_mile) run from Wisconsin plants to WCSB distribution centres (pr_cn_2014). Loading wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Railcars travel to the in-basin terminal
steps.description: The railway moves the cars from Wisconsin or other origins about 2,700 km to the terminal in northwest Alberta or northeast BC, with interchanges and yard holds along the way.

evidence.note: Route described in pr_cn_2014; transit of 5 to 17 days is the author's estimate for a Wisconsin to northern Alberta move.

steps.name: Track railcars and chase the railway
steps.description: Each day the coordinator downloads car positions from the railway and supplier portals into the sand plan, flags cars that have not moved for two days and phones the railway or supplier about them. They warn the last-mile desk when arrival dates slip.

error.defect_description: A stalled car is missed until the terminal runs short.

evidence.note: Rail line interruptions and railcar availability are named supply risks (source_q4_2018, source_q4_2022). Daily tracking effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Manage rail delay or bunching
steps.description: When cars stall in a cold snap or a yard, or arrive in a bunch the terminal cannot unload, the coordinator arranges sand from another terminal or the supplier's in-basin stock for the pad and asks the supply chain manager to approve the extra trucking or storage charges. They re-plan the pad's sand by day.

error.defect_description: Recovery plan double-counts sand that another pad needs.

evidence.note: Weather and rail interruptions named as risks (source_q4_2018); extreme cold delays in January 2022 (step_2021). Durations are estimates.

steps.name: Terminal spots and unloads railcars
steps.description: The terminal operator places the cars on its unloading tracks, empties them into silos by mesh and reports tonnes unloaded. Cars wait in the yard when the tracks or silos are full.

evidence.note: A typical terminal has three unloading tracks of 44 cars (fw_dicorp_2013); wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Post railcar receipt to terminal inventory
steps.description: The inventory controller keys the terminal's unload report into the ERP as a goods receipt against the release, by car and tonnes, so the sand shows as company stock at that terminal. They compare car tonnes with the bills of lading and flag shortfalls.

error.defect_description: Tonnes mis-keyed or posted to the wrong terminal.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: goods receipt before supplier invoice is paid

next.condition: receiving sample required for this lot

evidence.note: Receipt re-keyed from terminal reports is the author's description; sampling frequency is an estimate.

steps.name: Allocate terminal stock to the pad
steps.description: The coordinator reserves the tonnes by mesh for the pad in the sand plan, sends the last-mile desk the terminal, tonnes and pick-up authority, and tells the terminal which carrier will collect. This hands the sand to the hauling process.

error.defect_description: Mesh allocated to the wrong pad.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Arrange receiving sample
steps.description: The coordinator asks the terminal to pull a composite sample from the new lot and ship it to the company laboratory in Calgary with the car numbers, and logs the request.

evidence.note: Lab testing of sand is described in the organisation file; this request step is the author's description.

steps.name: Review sieve and crush result
steps.description: When the lab posts the result, the procurement specialist compares sieve distribution, crush resistance and turbidity with the supply agreement specification and decides whether the lot can be used.

control.basis: Supply agreement quality specification for frac sand (sieve and crush testing to ISO 13503-2 / API RP 19C)

evidence.note: Out-of-specification share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Rebalance stock after a program change
steps.description: When the customer delays, cancels or re-designs the pad, the coordinator works out where the reserved sand can go instead: another pad fed from the same terminal, a rail or truck transfer to another terminal, or storage until the pad restarts. They price each option.

evidence.note: Program changes leaving sand surplus at one terminal are named in the organisation file; share and effort are estimates.

steps.name: Release empty railcars and check demurrage
steps.description: The coordinator confirms with the terminal that the emptied cars have been released back to the railway or lessor and checks the railway's storage and demurrage notices for cars held too long, disputing charges caused by the railway.

evidence.note: Fixed railcar lease costs weigh on unit costs when cars sit (source_q4_2018); effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Raise quality claim and quarantine lot
steps.description: The procurement specialist asks the terminal to quarantine the silo, sends the lab result to the supplier with a claim, and agrees either replacement sand or a price concession that the design engineer accepts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide on transfer or storage
steps.description: The supply chain manager reviews the options, the terminal storage charges and the take-or-pay position, and decides whether to re-allocate, transfer or hold the sand.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for unbudgeted freight and storage costs

next.condition: held in terminal for a later pad

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm quantities for sand and freight invoices
steps.description: When the supplier's sand, rail freight and terminal invoices reach accounts payable, the procurement specialist confirms tonnes, price and surcharges against the release and the goods receipt, and explains any differences so the invoice can be paid.

control.basis: Three-way match: buyer confirms, accounts payable pays

evidence.note: Organisation file names buyers resolving differences with accounts payable; minutes are estimates.

exceptions.name: Supplier allocation cut
exceptions.description: The supplier cannot ship a mesh in the week asked, so the buyer re-sources or accepts a later date.

exceptions.name: Rail delay or bunching
exceptions.description: Cars stall in cold weather or arrive together; sand is borrowed from another terminal and trucking costs rise.

exceptions.name: Out-of-specification lot
exceptions.description: Lab testing finds the sand outside the sieve or crush specification; the silo is quarantined and replaced or discounted.

exceptions.name: Program change
exceptions.description: The customer delays or cancels the pad and the reserved sand is re-allocated, transferred or stored.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from pad requirement to invoice cleared
benchmarks.population: Releases of WCSB frac sand railed from Wisconsin or northern mines, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about one week of ordering and loading, one to two and a half weeks of rail transit, and one week of receipt and invoice clearing; releases filled from in-basin stock take a few days.

benchmarks.population: STEP Energy Services Canadian fracturing, Q4 2021 and full year 2021

evidence.note: Trade press figure for US unit trains.

pain_points.description: Sand plans live in spreadsheets fed by portals and emailed terminal reports, so stock figures are a day old and differ between coordinators.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Rail transit of two to three weeks means releases are committed before the customer's pad dates are firm; program changes then leave sand stranded at the wrong terminal.

evidence.note: Long rail haul from Wisconsin (pr_cn_2014) and demand swings with spring break-up timing (source_q4_2018).

pain_points.description: Cold weather and railcar shortages delay cars in winter, the busiest season, forcing costly truck transfers between terminals.

sources.title: Source Energy Services Reports Q4 2018 and Year End Results, Amendment to Normal Course Issuer Bid and Other Matters
sources.supports: In-basin frac sand transload terminal network; Fox Creek first unit-train-capable terminal in the Duvernay; Wembley expanded to dual-unit-train capability; 2,560,855 tonnes sold in 2018, 90% into the WCSB; last-mile trucking and Sahara wellsite storage; contracts directly with five producers; fixed railcar lease costs; risks of rail line interruptions, reduced railcar availability and weather; demand affected by the timing of spring break-up.

sources.title: Source Energy Services Reports Q4 2022 and Year End Results
sources.supports: 2,845,600 tonnes of sand sold in 2022, up 15% on 2021; last-mile trucking volumes fell in Q4 2022 because of customer job and permitting delays while longer terminal-to-wellsite trips raised revenue; higher repairs on the railcar fleet; supply contracts renewed with pricing reflecting the 2022 environment; risks of rail line interruptions and reduced railcar availability.

sources.title: Source Energy Services - home page
sources.supports: Frac sand supply and well completion chemicals in the WCSB through in-basin terminals; first company in Canada to offer unit-train-capable terminals; last-mile logistics; Sahara wellsite sand storage.

sources.title: Frac sand: CN begins to serve another Wisconsin plant; Claim Post touts Manitoba reserves
sources.supports: CN launched unit-train frac sand service between Wisconsin production facilities and distribution centres in northwestern Alberta and northeastern BC; CN expected 82,000 frac sand carloads in 2014, up from 55,000 in 2013.

sources.title: CN to haul frac sand to Alberta transload facility
sources.supports: Di-Corp transload terminal at Grande Prairie served by CN: 20 acres, annual capacity 550,000 tons of frac sand, three unloading tracks of 44 rail cars each; sand from the US Midwest and Manitoba; terminal adds offloading and storage capacity at destination.

sources.title: 'Last Mile' Solutions Enhance Efficiency, Reliability Of Proppant Supply Chain (K. Fisher)
sources.supports: Pneumatic truck about 46,000 lb; pneumatic unloading 40-70 minutes, about 45 minutes on average; about a dozen trucks typically queued at the pad; one pad can need more than 130 truckloads a day; carriers bill stand-by or demurrage when trucks wait; shipment tracking through phone apps instead of calls between dispatchers, carriers and terminals; last mile up to a third of delivered sand cost; rail cars of 200,000-220,000 lb and unit trains of 110-120 cars. US conditions in 2017.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing: 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant in 2021 (776,000 in 2020), 977 operating days, proppant per stage 54 tonnes (Q4 2021) to 83 tonnes (2021); product and hauling costs rose with company-supplied proppant; costs rose late in 2021 with supply chain disruptions; weather delays in late December 2021 and extreme cold in January 2022; spring break-up restricts equipment moves; US segment cites inflation on chemicals, proppant and spare parts.

sources.title: Hydraulic Fracturing
sources.supports: Service covers engineering design through procurement and coordination of chemicals, proppants, people and equipment; secure supply of proppants; ceramic proppants sourced on request; full suite of friction reducers and a full line of chemical and fluid systems; high-concentration slickwater products to streamline logistics; full-service lab in Calgary.

assumptions: The company buys most sand under term agreements priced FOB the in-basin terminal or at the mine with rail freight passed through; customer-supplied sand is outside this process.
A release covers one pad or terminal top-up of 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes; about 38% of pad requirements are met from stock already in basin with no new release.
Rail transit times, terminal waits and touch times are the author's estimates; no published Canadian frac sand transit benchmark was found.
Laboratory testing itself belongs to the quality testing process; here only the request and the review of the result appear.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).
Invoice clearing is included because buyers confirm sand and freight quantities for accounts payable; the payment run itself belongs to accounts payable.
